text:
maria: Quick sync — after the kernel-selector switch rolled last night I'm seeing a notable increase in cross-region queue spill and token budget drain for EU. 95p latency up ~180ms. Anyone else seeing noisy tails?

jonathan: Yep, noticed EU-north p95 jump around 23:10 UTC. KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% around the same time. Suspect cache locality changed. :thinking:

sasha: I'm pulling traces now. Initial flamegraph shows more remote KV fetches during batch formation. Link: https://internal.perf/fg/18525 (will attach).

kevin: FWIW the kernel selector change was: `kernel_selector: auto_v2 -> auto_v3` and a small batching tweak that relaxed zone affinity to favor larger batch sizes. Config diff: 
```
- queue_policy.affinity: HARD
- queue_policy.preferred_zone_match: true
+ queue_policy.affinity: SOFT
+ queue_policy.preferred_zone_match: false
```

maria: That matches my hypothesis — we loosened affinity to increase throughput but it looks like KV cache locality loss > throughput gains for small chat workloads.

jonathan: I captured a short trace. Key snippet from scheduler log: 
```
[23:09:58] schedule: batch_id=766 model=redwood-7b seq=64 zone=eu-north assigned_zone=eu-west spill=true tokens=12
[23:09:58] kvcache: miss_count=48 hit_count=112 hit_rate=0.70 (prev window 0.82)
```

sasha: Running a quick sim with synthetic arrival distribution. Early results: when affinity is SOFT, cross-zone assignment increases by ~22% and avg KV fetch latency goes up 15ms, which cascades into smaller effective batch sizes.

kevin: Does the kernel change also alter KV cache sharding/hash? I thought it only selected compute kernels.

maria: Kernel change shouldn't touch sharding, but the batching heuristic change did — we now group by model+priority only, not zone+model. That means batches are assembled across queues more aggressively, causing remote KV access.

sasha: I captured profiler output for KV RPCs. Top 3 callers = `kv_get_prefix`, `kv_load_block`, `kv_prefetch`. Prefetches dropped from 60% success -> 35% success after change.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: region=eu North p95 latency increased 18% at 1852499000. Triggered checks: kvcache_hit_rate, batch_size_avg, cross_zone_spill_rate.

maria: Action proposal: revert affinity relaxation in staging, re-run traffic sim with token_budget targets {8,16} and measure p95 and kvcache hit. If revert recovers hit-rate, we need a soft-tunable that biases by zone when kvcache hit < 80%.

jonathan: I'll run the sim with both token_budgets and also toggle `kv_prefetch.window_ms` to see sensitivity. CMD I'm using: `./tools/queue-sim --trace=eu-24h.json --policy=soft|hard --token_budget=8,16`

sasha: Running kvcache profiler on staging now. ETA ~12m. Posting partials when ready.

kevin: I'll prepare a small patch that exposes `queue_policy.zone_bias` in runtime config and default it to 0.25 so we can experiment without full revert. Patch diff ready locally.

maria: Good. Also we need to add a regression test in perf harness that asserts kvcache_hit_rate >= 0.78 for typical chat trace with 95% traffic local region.

jonathan: Agree. I'll add test and run overnight suite. If we can detect token siphoning (lots of small cross-zone batches), we'll flag and auto-raise zone_bias.

sasha: Profiler partials: prefetch success now shown per-batch: [0.34,0.36,0.31,0.37]. Definitely down. Attaching logs excerpt: 
```
batch 766: assigns: [eu-west, eu-north, eu-north] kv_prefetchs=9 success=3
batch 767: assigns: [eu-north, eu-west] kv_prefetchs=6 success=2
```

maria: OK let's do this plan: (1) kevin deploys zone_bias flag to staging with default 0.5 (2) sasha re-runs profiler + sim (3) jonathan runs perf harness A/B with token_budget 8 vs 16 and collects p95 + kvcache_hit. Report back in ~30m. @kevin please kick off the staging deploy. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Starting deploy to staging: runtime/affinity-zone-bias flag=0.5 (build 2026.3.1852). Rolling 10 nodes.

kevin: Deploy kicked. Watching logs.

maria: Thanks team. If revert needed we revert the batching-policy change and push patch to make zone_bias adaptive. We'll reconvene after results.

jonathan: I'll post simulation results in this thread when done.

sasha: Partial: staging with zone_bias=0.5 shows kvcache hit ~0.80 and cross-zone assigns dropped to 6% (from 22%). Early p95 improvement seen.

maria: Nice. Keep an eye on throughput delta. We can't kill throughput for tiny savings.

kevin: Noted — initial numbers show throughput down ~4% but p95 improved. Patch will include telemetry to iterate.

maria: Great. We'll capture these in the release notes and tie a Optimize suggestion: "Enable zone_bias when kvcache_hit < X". Closing loop after full runs. :white_check_mark:
